# Governance

Paper & Slate publishes documentation from a local, reviewable source set. This page records the boundaries that are
currently evidenced by the documentation system; it is not a claim of institutional approval or production status.

## Source review

Central pages are reviewed repository-owned Markdown. Each ingested page retains its source path, local ref, and
content hash. Fixture, sibling-local, and future Git-imported pages remain separated from the reviewed central rendering
path.

## Versions and provenance

Supported and historical versions remain independent records. A content hash identifies the recorded bytes; it is not
presented as a Git commit SHA. Raw Markdown routes remain available for source inspection.

## Honest status

Local checks can establish source shape, route behavior, rendering boundaries, and generated artifacts. They do not by
themselves establish deployment, legal review, provider activation, production monitoring, or factual approval.

# Data Platform boundary note

**Status: Planned and non-accepting.** This note records a local ownership boundary; it is not a Data Platform contract or canonical-record receipt.

The Course and Catalog Schema proposal describes catalog-facing labels and relationships only. Its `courseId`, `catalogId`, lifecycle labels, and provenance do not establish enrollment, learner state, completion, credit, accreditation, credentials, a source catalog, an API, or an immutable release.

Data Platform retains canonical education data, learner/enrollment state, provenance stores, APIs, and release semantics. Any future projection or compatibility request requires a Data-owned versioned contract receipt; this workspace makes no acceptance claim.

**Status: Planned.** A course record could describe title, summary, audience, prerequisites, and catalog relationships. It must not imply enrollment, credit, accreditation, or completion without separately verified facts.

Read the Planned descriptive record proposal for local identifiers, relationships, lifecycle/effective dates, explicit unknowns, claim boundaries, and synthetic fixture rules.

The [Data Platform boundary note](/docs/standards-course-schema/data-boundary) is non-accepting and does not define a canonical data contract.

Standards owns this local descriptive proposal. Data Platform owns canonical education data and release semantics; this page does not accept that contract.

# Registry and Data boundary dossier

**Status: Experimental and non-accepting.** This dossier records a requested ownership boundary; it is not a Standards Registry or Data Platform receipt.

This local proposal uses synthetic framework identifiers and local snapshots only. It does not ingest official standards, resolve mappings, assert conformance, establish source rights, or publish a framework release. `candidate-only`, `unresolved`, `unknown`, and `tentative` states must remain visible.

Standards Registry owns official framework sources, rights review, canonical framework models, mappings, workbench/API behavior, evidence stores, and releases. Data Platform owns canonical education data, provenance stores, APIs, and release semantics. EOM retains protocol identity and authority. Any future projection, ingestion, or compatibility request remains unaccepted until the owning project supplies its own versioned receipt.

# EOM boundary dossier

**Status: Experimental and non-accepting.** This dossier documents a local compatibility boundary; it is not an EOM contract, implementation, endorsement, or acceptance record.

The Education Discovery proposal does not define or publish a `.well-known` endpoint, reuse EOM normative identifiers, claim IANA registration, assert interoperability, or establish identity, authority, capability, schema, or release semantics. Its `discoveryId` is a local descriptive label and its hashes describe synthetic workspace snapshots only.

EOM retains ownership of protocol identity, authority, capability semantics, schemas, endpoints, registration, conformance, and release identity. A future compatibility or adapter request requires an immutable EOM owner receipt and a fresh review from that owner; this local validator cannot substitute for either.

Standards Registry and Data Platform retain official-source, rights, canonical, mapping, API, and release authority. Web owns public ingestion and publication, UI owns runtime acceptance, and Documents owns file-format semantics and materialization. No sibling acceptance, legal conclusion, adoption, certification, provider activation, or production behavior is inferred here.

The only local evidence is the deterministic validator and its synthetic vectors. Keep unresolved identity, route, review, provenance, and interoperability states explicit, and stop if a proposed change crosses one of these ownership boundaries.

title: .well-known Education Discovery

# .well-known Education Discovery

**Status: Experimental.** The local discovery proposal describes education-shaped resources and documentation paths without publishing a network endpoint or asserting ecosystem support. Its machine-readable profile is discovery-record.schema.json, with synthetic valid and invalid vectors under fixtures.

## Ownership

Standards owns this Experimental descriptive proposal. EOM owns any `.well-known` protocol contract, endpoint, registration, conformance, and release.

The [EOM boundary dossier](/docs/standards-discovery/eom-boundary) records the non-accepting compatibility and authority split. Registry, Data Platform, Web, UI, and Documents retain their own source, rights, runtime, acceptance, publication, and file-format boundaries.

## Verification

Run `pnpm verify` from the Standards root, `node scripts/validate-discovery.mjs`, and `node --test tests/discovery`. Local checks do not prove interoperability, registration, publication, rights, or production readiness.

## Documentation

See the project README for audience, non-goals, contribution, and evidence limits.

## Safety boundary

Consumers should treat discovery as descriptive metadata and verify source provenance before relying on it.

# License and endorsement boundary

**Status: Planned and non-accepting.** This note records local inventory boundaries; it is not a rights, security, provider, or support receipt.

An inventory `listed` state means only that descriptive text exists in this local workspace. It does not mean installed, available, supported, endorsed, secure, certified, provider-activated, or legally cleared. `licenseReference.scope: descriptive-only` is a pointer for review, never a license grant or conclusion about redistribution rights.

Provider, security, support, and rights owners retain their own acceptance authority. Consumers must perform independent due diligence; no dependency installation, provider call, public publication, or sibling contract is performed here.
